internal/transport/ws.go:s.runPaneObserv: the pane-observation coalescer (nocx-szb40.3): exactly ONE per server, started by Start and ended by Stop, which closes sweepDone and then WAITS on sweepExited — so a returned Stop means no sweep is still running. Its earlier form ended only on the context Start was given, which is not the server lifetime; in this package tests that is context.Background(), and the ticker outlived every server that wired an observer (nocx-2h08 is the neighbourhood that makes a leaked periodic goroutine expensive here). It is not a handler goroutine and escapes none of the four accountings: no admission, no domain ownership, no caller waiting on it, every send the same non-blocking TryNotify a handler would use. It exists because the alternative is classifying on the session read path, which is the hot path of every session in the product: an agent pane repaints its token counter on every response chunk, so that would run a VT scan per chunk. Touch marks a pane dirty there and does nothing else; this loop turns dirty into a classification, and only a CHANGE is sent.

internal/transport/ws_download.go:s.emit: the running transfer's progress emitter (upload design §5.3, and the download half of nocx-9le.8.1 unchanged): exactly one per transfer in EITHER direction, started beside s.runUpload or s.runDownload and ending when that transfer's done channel closes, so it is bounded in number by maxTransfers and in time by the transfer it belongs to — the same lifetime and the same accounting as the transfer goroutine beside it, which is already baselined. It exists because the alternative is worse in both directions: the engine's copy loop calls progress once per 256 KiB chunk, so marshalling and enqueueing there would put that work on the write path thousands of times a second and fill the connection's refreshable queue (outbound.DefaultQueueDepth = 256), which does not merely drop frames but trips the stall notice the renderer treats as a cue to reconnect. This goroutine reads a single-slot mailbox instead, so a burst of chunks collapses into one notification carrying the newest byte count and at most one is ever outstanding per transfer. It escapes none of the four accountings: it holds no admission and no domain ownership, it answers no caller, every send is a non-blocking TryNotify that is dropped rather than retried, and shutdown accounts for it — WSServer.Stop calls cancelAllTransfers, and a cancelled transfer closes rt.done, which is this loop's only exit.
internal/transport/ws_download.go:s.runD: the running download (upload design D8, in the read direction): a transfer routinely outlives the call that started it — a 2 GB download over a slow link is a working download — so files.download pins the file, mints a ticket and returns. What the goroutine carries is the binding's SOURCE and the already-open handle, and nothing else: the filesystem handle and its use-guard are both let go when the RPC answers, so files.close, session teardown and shutdown cancel it, wait a bounded moment and then close for real rather than draining a guard the transfer still holds. It does NOT escape the four accountings: it carries its own context, owned by the transfer and bounded by its session; the admission it leaves is deliberate and is the decision itself; it answers no caller, so nothing is left waiting on it; and shutdown accounts for it — WSServer.Stop calls cancelAllTransfers, which cancels every transfer in both directions and waits, bounded, before the drain. Bounded in number by maxTransfers. Its one obligation beyond the upload's is the pinned handle: the deferred Close on this goroutine is the only place that descriptor is released, on every path including the one where nobody ever fetched.
internal/transport/ws_end_hold.go:func(): the end hold's deferred boundary consult (nocx-zg3k3.5.11 Round 4): at most one per consult site per re-adopt — the two AttachBlockRows entries and the re-adopt tail — started by settleWhenEndHoldLifts only when a hold is armed, and ended by the hold's lift, whose every release path closes a channel it selects on (the drain closes with the window's head or the attachment's end; released closes on integration loss, a re-arm, or the teardown consuming the hold). It cannot run inline: its callers are inside the re-attachment callback and the reconcile pass, and blocking either would stall the very replay the hold waits for (StartLifecycle runs after the callback returns). Not control-handler work and it escapes none of the four accountings: nothing is admitted, no caller waits on a reply from it, no domain ownership is taken; its one effect is the idempotent settle the exit's own post-hold settle also runs.

the ring-to-connection relay on attach: replays buffered output to the newly attached subscriber on its own goroutine, cancelled by the connection context. It runs on the CONNECTION's context (pumpCtx) rather than the request's, because the relay outlives the handler that started it and must die with the socket (nocx-3an1s.2.2).

the reattach relay: a second connection taking over a session starts its own replay goroutine, cancelled by its own connection context and by losing the subscriber slot (D8). It runs on the connection's context for the same reason as the attach relay above: a rebind's relay must outlive the rebind request and end with its socket.
